items.title: What would Amendment 3’s property tax cut mean for Miami-Dade homeowners?
items.desc: Florida voters are deciding whether to raise state’s homestead tax exemption, which would lower property taxes but may affect buyers.

headlines: AMENDMENT 3 COULD SAVE MIAMI HOMEOWNERS THOUSANDS IN TAXES
BIG TAX CUTS COULD IMPACT MIAMI-DADE SERVICES
WILL MIAMI-DADE TRADE PUBLIC SERVICES FOR LOWER TAX BILLS?
draft.article:
Miami-Dade voters will decide on Amendment 3 on the Nov. 3 ballot, a measure that would significantly increase Florida's homestead tax exemption for longtime residents.

If passed, the non-school exemption would jump from $50,000 to $150,000 in 2027, and reach $250,000 in 2028 for primary homeowners living in the state before the end of 2026. Florida TaxWatch estimates this change would save city of Miami homeowners $1,216 in 2027 and $2,448 in 2028.

However, the Florida Policy Institute projects Miami-Dade County would lose $1.5 billion across fiscal years 2028 and 2029. Local transit, trash pickup, libraries, and Jackson Health System, which projects a $64 million funding loss, could face cutbacks.

Dieppa has been selected as the new police chief for the City of Mount Dora, City Manager Vince Sandersfeld announced. Dieppa previously served as chief of the Chamblee Police Department in Georgia and holds a doctorate in education in leadership and innovation. He replaces former chief Michael Gibson, who retired after a 36-year law enforcement career. Deputy Chief James Deleu has served as acting chief during the transition. Officials expect Dieppa to begin his new leadership duties in early December, with formal swearing-in details to follow.

items.title: Hialeah Paid Mayor Calvo's Own Consultant $13K to Text About His Events

headlines: HIALEAH PAID MAYOR CALVO'S CAMPAIGN STRATEGIST THOUSANDS FOR MASS TEXTS
THOUSANDS SPENT ON MAYOR TEXTS WITHOUT COUNCIL KNOWLEDGE
WHY ARE HIALEAH TAX DOLLARS FUNDING TEXTS PROMOTING MAYOR EVENTS?
draft.article:
The City of Hialeah paid $13,050 to Dark Horse Strategies and Consulting Inc., a political consulting firm run by Mayor Bryan Calvo's former campaign strategist, Emiliano Antunez. Between April and July, the firm sent thousands of mass texts promoting Calvo's public appearances, starting just three months after he took office.

The text campaigns covered events such as an Earth Day cleanup, a town hall, a Fourth of July celebration, and the Mayor's Cup Fan Fest. Other texts promoted Cortaditos with the Mayor and the reopening of Bucky Dent Water Park.

Hialeah City Council members were unaware of the payments. However, the total stays beneath the city's $25,000 threshold that mandates council approval.

headlines: AMENDMENT 3 PROPOSES MASSIVE HOMESTEAD EXEMPTION HIKE THIS NOVEMBER
MIAMI-DADE LEADERS SPLIT OVER TAX CUTS
COULD AMENDMENT 3 DRAIN HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS FROM MIAMI-DADE?
draft.article: Miami-Dade leaders are divided over Amendment 3 ahead of the November vote. The measure would raise Florida's homestead exemption from $50,000 to $250,000 by 2028, needing 60% voter approval to pass. County Mayor Daniella Levine Cava opposes the proposal. She warns Miami-Dade could lose $378 million in year one and nearly $700 million in year two, threatening funding for transit, libraries, parks, and fire stations. District 11 Commissioner Roberto J. Gonzalez backs the amendment, arguing it trims bloated government and restores affordability by returning money to residents. Meanwhile, Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz contends tax relief and public safety can coexist.

headlines: DADE COUNTY WAS CREATED ON FEBRUARY 4, 1836
MIAMI HISTORY: DADE COUNTY FORMED IN 1836
THE 1836 ORIGINS OF DADE COUNTY AND FORT DALLAS
draft.article:
Dade County officially came into existence on February 4, 1836, marking the formal beginning of our local jurisdiction. The new county was named in honor of Major Francis L. Dade and the Miami River.

That same year, Fort Dallas was established along the riverbanks. The fort immediately took on a strategic defense role, operating as an active military base throughout the Second Seminole War.

From the historic grounds of Fort Dallas to the designation along the Miami River, the foundational events of 1836 established the local community and defined the early territory of Dade County.
